title: isDue() and repo.listDue() implement due-ness two different ways
detail: srs.isDue parses the timestamp; repo.listDue string-compares ISO text. They agree only while every dueAt is UTC Z-format. Two sources of truth for the single question the whole review feature turns on.

title: A card with an unparseable dueAt is invisible forever
detail: Date.parse returns NaN and NaN <= now is false, so the card is never due, never surfaces, and is never cleaned up — it just sits in the store inflating counts.

title: INTERVAL_MODIFIER[1] is dead
detail: grade===1 short-circuits to a literal 1 before the modifier table is consulted, so the 0 entry can never be read.

title: dateRead is parsed from the CSV and then thrown away
detail: GoodreadsRow carries dateRead, but importGoodreadsRows never maps it to Book.finishedAt. Every imported Finished book therefore has no completion date, which is exactly what the monthly reading goal needs.

title: coverForIsbn omits ?default=false, so unknown ISBNs render a blank image
detail: OpenLibrary serves a 1x1 transparent placeholder rather than a 404 for ISBNs it does not hold. Without default=false the URL always looks valid, so the local placeholder fallback is never reached and imported books show an empty cover.

title: Imported rating is never clamped to 0-5
detail: Any finite integer in the My Rating column is stored verbatim and rendered as stars.

title: No timeout on any cover fetch
detail: Both providers await bare fetch with no AbortSignal. A hung request stalls fetchCover, which sits in the critical path of summarizeBook, so a slow third party blocks book creation indefinitely.

title: Cover lookups are uncached and cost up to 3 network round trips each
detail: fetchGoogleBooksCover alone issues two sequential queries. getAIRecommendations Promise.all's six of these, so one refresh can fire eighteen requests, repeated for the same titles on every refresh.

title: bytesToBase64 converts a whole PDF on the main thread
detail: A per-byte loop plus btoa over a multi-megabyte buffer blocks rendering for seconds with no chunking and no yield.

title: revokeObjectURL runs synchronously after click(), which can cancel the download
detail: Firefox in particular has not necessarily begun reading the blob when the same task revokes the URL. The usual fix is to defer the revoke a tick.

title: slugify can leave a trailing hyphen
detail: Trim runs before the 60-char slice, so a truncation landing on a separator produces filenames ending in '-'.

title: Malformed quiz JSON silently yields zero questions
detail: data.questions ?? [] turns a shape failure into an empty quiz. The user sees an empty modal rather than an explanation, and zero review cards are created.

title: One failing cover lookup discards all six recommendations
detail: Promise.all rejects as a whole, losing the entire paid response.

title: API key changes in another tab are never observed
detail: The module keeps its own listener set but never subscribes to the window storage event, so a key added in a second tab leaves the first tab still gating AI actions.

title: Odd-length PCM is written as a valid 16-bit stream
detail: A truncated final sample produces a header claiming more complete samples than the data contains.

title: Every generated audio blob URL leaks for the life of the page
detail: createObjectURL is handed to onPlayAudio and never revoked. Combined with the absence of audio caching, each Quick Listen both re-bills a TTS call and pins another full WAV in memory until reload.

title: handleOpenPdf leaks a blob URL per click
detail: createObjectURL feeds window.open and is never revoked. PDFs are the largest objects the app holds, so repeatedly opening one walks memory up with no ceiling.

title: Quick Listen and Read Full Summary render for unsummarised books and silently do nothing
detail: Both handlers set their spinner, then hit `if (!summary) return`. Chat and Quiz are correctly gated behind `summary &&` at line 342, but these two are not — so the spinner flashes and nothing happens, with no explanation.

title: The One Sentence Takeaway panel is unreadable in dark mode
detail: The panel background flips (bg-orange-50 dark:bg-orange-950/50) but text-orange-800 and text-orange-900 carry no dark variant, leaving near-black text on a near-black panel.

title: SummaryRenderer body text has no dark variant
detail: The wrapper is text-gray-800 with no dark: pairing, so the entire rendered summary — the main content of the page — stays dark grey on a dark background. Same omission at lines 46, 483 and 501.

title: Deep-dive loading panel and the Move back to Queue button are light-only
detail: bg-stone-50 / text-stone-900 / text-stone-500 and bg-stone-100 / text-stone-600 have no dark variants. The Phase 3 dark-mode pass covered gray-* and white but missed stone-* and amber-* entirely.

title: Marking a book Finished never records finishedAt
detail: toggleStatus writes status and rating only. This is the manual counterpart to the Goodreads gap in S024 — between them, nothing in the app ever populates finishedAt, so the monthly reading goal can never count anything.

title: Personal notes save on blur only, so unmounting mid-edit loses them
detail: Browser back, a keyboard route change, or closing the tab unmounts the textarea without firing onBlur. The 'Auto-saves when you click away' label overstates what is actually guaranteed.

title: Cover image has no onError fallback
detail: A dead cover URL — which S025 makes likely for every Goodreads import — renders the browser's broken-image glyph instead of falling back to placeholderCover.

title: A hand-rolled markdown renderer lives inside a component file
detail: formatInline and SummaryRenderer are ~80 lines of parsing logic with array-index keys, embedded in the page component rather than in lib/ where the project's other pure transforms live and where they could be tested.
